findings.defect: The English uses an unnatural collocation and obscures the straightforward point that the visitor is late for the agreed time.
findings.rationale: 약속했던 시간을 어겼습니다 means that he failed to arrive at the promised time, not that he literally “broke” time.

findings.current: The middle-aged man wearing a Taegeukgi pin on his chest was entitled to do so.
findings.defect: Taegeukgi is unnecessarily romanized without an established ledger entry or explanatory footnote.
findings.rationale: 태극기 is the national flag of Korea and has a clear, natural English rendering here.
findings.replacement: The middle-aged man wearing a Korean flag pin on his chest was entitled to do so.
findings.source: 가슴에 태극기 배지를 단 중년인은 그래도 되는 사람이었다.

findings.current: “It’s been a while, Vice Guild Master Lee. Is this our first meeting since your inauguration ceremony at the beginning of the year?”
findings.defect: The possessive reverses the subject of the inauguration: Baek Hanseong, not Lee Jungryong, took office and swore the presidential oath.
findings.rationale: 취임 선서 refers to President Baek Hanseong’s own oath of office, as confirmed by the surrounding discussion of the first year of his presidential term.
findings.replacement: “It’s been a while, Vice Guild Master Lee. Is this the first time we’ve met since I took the oath of office at the beginning of the year?”
findings.source: “오랜만입니다. 이정룡 부길드장님. 올해 초 취임 선서 때 뵙고 처음인가요?”

findings.current: *The previous president never once visited the Blue House during his term.*
findings.defect: The translation assigns the action to the previous president, but the omitted subject is Lee Jungryong. The point is that Lee refused to visit the previous administration.
findings.rationale: This thought explains why Baek’s ability to meet Lee, even unofficially, reflects Baek’s current political strength and their mutual interests.
findings.replacement: *Lee Jungryong never once visited the Blue House during the previous president’s term.*
findings.source: ‘전임 대통령 집권 당시에는 청와대를 단 한 번도 방문하지 않았었지.’

findings.current: “A Lich, was it? That Named Monster ended up helping China’s Central Committee, albeit unintentionally. I hear even American satellites can’t see what’s happening inside.”
findings.defect: The draft does not use the binding established rendering for 미국.
findings.rationale: The terminology ledger establishes United States for 미국.
findings.replacement: “A Lich, was it? That Named Monster ended up helping China’s Central Committee, albeit unintentionally. I hear even satellites from the United States can’t see what’s happening inside.”
findings.source: “리치(Lich)라고 하던가요? 그 네임드 몬스터가 의도치 않게 중국 중앙위원회를 도운 셈이 됐습니다. 미국 인공위성으로도 내부를 파악할 수 없다고 하니 말입니다.”

findings.current: “As you know, China’s Hunters are not particularly well trained for an army of that size.”
findings.defect: The draft turns the comparison with China’s large Hunter population into a reference to an army’s size and reduces 정예화, the development of elite personnel, to generic training.
findings.rationale: The source contrasts the sheer number of Hunters China possesses with its inadequate elite-level strength, which explains why it needs foreign high-ranking Hunters.
findings.replacement: “As you know, China has a great many Hunters, but relatively few of them are truly elite.”
findings.source: “부길드장님께서도 익히 아시겠지만, 중국은 보유한 헌터의 머릿수에 비해 정예화가 그리 잘 되어 있지 않습니다.”

findings.current: “The Peace Guild is a very small operation, so perhaps that’s why they prepared so quickly. They should already be boarding their flight by now.”
findings.defect: The progressive “be boarding” changes the source’s completed action: Baek expects them already to have boarded.
findings.rationale: 이미 항공편에 탑승했을 겁니다 indicates that boarding should already be complete.
findings.replacement: “The Peace Guild is a very small operation, so perhaps that’s why they prepared so quickly. They should already be aboard their flight by now.”
findings.source: “평화 길드는 워낙 영세한 곳이라 그런지, 준비도 빠르더군요. 지금쯤이면 이미 항공편에 탑승했을 겁니다.”

findings.current: *It’s a shame, but please tell Chairman Jongseok I can’t go.*
findings.defect: The invented name Jongseok is part of a Korean sound-based joke but is presented without the required explanation, leaving it indistinguishable from an unestablished character name.
findings.rationale: 종석 deliberately mangles 주석, Xiao Yang’s title, into a personal name. A concise footnote preserves the joke without implying that Jongseok is a real person.
findings.replacement:
*It’s a shame, but please tell Chairman Jongseok[^1] I can’t go.*

[^1]: Taekyung twists the Korean title *juseok* (“chairman”) into the similar-sounding name Jongseok.
findings.source: ‘안타깝긴 한데, 종석이 아저씨한테 못 간다고 전해 주세요.’

findings.current: *A weekly wage? A weekly hundred billion?*
findings.defect: The amount is inflated tenfold. 백억 is ten billion won, not one hundred billion won.
findings.rationale: The preceding offer and this astonished repetition both state 백억, or ten billion won; the stretched 백어억 conveys Taekyung’s incredulous delivery rather than a different amount.
findings.replacement: *Weekly pay? T-ten billion won a week?*

summary: The draft contains two critical subject reversals, one critical quantity error, and several localized fidelity and terminology issues.
